terms.gloss: the filling: the mixture spooned between the layers or put inside
evidence: Apic. 4.2.14: tot trullās impēnsae dēsuper adjiciēs
terms.comment: Apicius’s word for the mixture a cook spoons between the layers of a patina or stuffs into gourds; it is also the materials of a dish (see “ingredients”). In Cato’s cakes the cheese and honey spread between the sheets of pastry are not given a name.

evidence: Col. 5.10.11: fartum fīcī plēniōrem ac meliōrem
terms.comment: What is stuffed into something (see “stuffing”); Columella uses it for the soft inside of a fig.

phrases.english: Taste the filling: is it sweet enough?

phrases.latin: Impēnsa nōndum crassa est; paulum adhūc coque.
phrases.english: The filling isn’t thick yet; cook it a little longer.

phrases.latin: Quotquot lagana posueris, tot trullās impēnsae dēsuper adjiciēs.
phrases.english: However many sheets of pastry you lay down, you will spoon as many ladlefuls of filling on top.

phrases.latin: Ea rēs efficit ūberiōrem frūctum et fartum fīcī plēniōrem ac meliōrem.
phrases.english: This gives a larger crop and makes the inside of the fig fuller and better.

sources: Lewis & Short: impendo · Lewis & Short: farcio
